name: Wunan Foundation
description:
Australia

Wunan Foundation was established in 1997 to improve the lives of Aboriginal people in the East Kimberley and drive sustainable change for the future. ‘Wunan’, a traditional ritual of Aboriginal people from the region, encompasses the idea of sharing and caring. With this mindset, Wunan works to achieve equality and long-term socioeconomic change. Its key areas of focus are: education, employment, housing, leadership, welfare reform and health.

The Problem

A number of root causes has resulted in long-term disadvantage for Aboriginal people in the East Kimberley. They are more likely to experience higher rates of chronic disease, unemployment and incarceration. Lack of opportunity has led to difficulties with education, employment and housing, as well as poor healthcare and substance abuse. These issues need to be addressed at a fundamental level in order to pave the way to a social and economic culture of support and opportunity.

The Solution

Wunan believes in providing opportunity and supporting the abilities of Aboriginal communities. With the right support, the unfair disadvantage faced by many Aboriginal people can change. Wunan Foundation’s programs include re-engaging students in school and training, increasing home ownership, providing career support, and running a driver’s license training program. Their main objective is to shift the balance of Aboriginal people dependent on welfare from 80% to 20% over the next 20 years. You can play a key part in making this happen.

What difference will your money make?

$150 provides a day’s Remote School Attendance transport service.

$320 gives a child a week’s worth of housing in a KEEP house.  

$480 provides a Wunan Foundation worker with a week of hostel accommodation.
